senses.gloss: m. (חוי, v. Ges. H. Dict.10 s. v. חוה) serpent.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 4:2">Targ. O. Ex. IV, 2</cite> <cite ref="H00683"><he>חִיוֵּי</he></cite> ed. Berl. (Var. <cite ref="H00683"><he>חֵיוִי</he></cite>, <cite ref="H00310"><he>חֵוֵי</he></cite>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 1:3:3">Y. Sabb. I, 3ᵇ</cite> <he>ודבר נשא ח׳</he> and the spine of a human being is turned into a serpent.
<cite ref="Shabbat 85a:2">Sabb. 85ᵃ</cite> (play on <he>הַחִוִּי</he>) <he>שהיו טועמין את הארץ כח׳</he> they tasted the ground (for agricultural purposes) like a serpent.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 20:12">Gen. R. s. 20</cite> (play on <cite ref="H00266"><he>חַוָּה</he></cite>) <he>ח׳ חִוְיָךְ ואת ח׳ דאדם</he> the serpent is thy (Eve’s) serpent (seducer), and thou art Adam’s serpent.

<cite ref="Shabbat 110a:8">Sabb. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>ח׳ דרבנן טרקיה</he> the Rabbis’ serpent bit him, i.e. he was bitten by a serpent as a punishment for disregarding rabbinical ordinances (with ref. to <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 10:8">Koh. X, 8</cite>); <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 27b:9">Ab. Zar. 27ᵇ</cite>.
Ber. 12ᵇ זקף כח׳ erected himself (in prayer) like a serpent (raising his head first); a. fr.—Pl. חִיוַּיָּא; (fem. pl.) חִיוָּן, חִיוָוָן, חִיוָיָן.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 21:6">Targ. Num. XXI, 6</cite>, sq.; a. fr.—[V. <cite ref="A00629"><he>אִוְיָא</he></cite>.]
